subject: POC trial: Acme Health - next steps & workload intake
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: Acme Health - next steps & workload intake

Hi Jordan — great to connect today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

Summary / success criteria (what a successful POC looks like)
- 95th percentile latency for inference < 300ms for production-like requests (per-token cost + latency target)
- Sustained throughput target: ~200 RPS baseline, support for bursts up to 500 RPS without >2s tail latency
- Quality: model outputs should match your acceptance tests for the triage use cases (we'll agree on 8 sample prompts)
- Integration: end-to-end inference from your staging environment to Redwood within 2 weeks

Evaluation plan / timeline
- Week 0: intake + kickoff (this week)
- Weeks 1-2: POC run with synthetic and masked sample traffic + evaluation harness
- End of week 2: review against acceptance tests and decide rollout path

Ownership
- Redwood: Ben (sales, overall), Marissa (solutions eng, POC lead)
- Acme Health: Jordan (product lead)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please fill the attached workload intake template (workload-intake-template.csv) with: avg RPS, peak RPS, burst duration, typical prompt/token lengths, concurrency, and any rate-limits.
2) Share 8 representative prompts and expected outputs (can be masked PHI).
3) Confirm preferred kickoff times for this week (Marissa will propose slots).

Attachments: [attachment: workload-intake-template.csv (CSV)]

If that looks right I'll have Marissa schedule the kickoff and we can lock in a start date.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: Acme Health - next steps & workload intake

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few details from our side to populate the intake: 

- Typical traffic: avg ~50 RPS during business hours (US EST), but we see bursts to ~500 RPS for 20-45s during peak events (e.g., daily digest).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~30-40 sessions; max observed ~300 concurrent sessions under load tests.
- Prompt lengths: typical user prompt = 80-140 tokens; combined context (prompt + system + response) avg ~420 tokens, max ~2,048 tokens for full context requests.
- Preferred SLA concerns: we need 99.9% availability during business hours and clear data retention/segregation for PHI. Procurement will follow up with a security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence, KMS details).

I'll get the intake filled today and share masked sample prompts. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports redaction workflows for PHI and what the default retention window is for logs?

—Jordan
Jordan Alvarez
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
jordan@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: Acme Health - next steps & workload intake

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the detail. Short answers: yes, we support configurable redaction hooks and can integrate your redaction pipeline prior to logging; default log retention for POCs is 30 days unless you request longer and we can add an enterprise retention addon. We'll flag procurement for SOC2/KMS scope — Marissa will own the evidence handoff.

Based on your numbers I've drafted the POC acceptance criteria: 
- Latency: 95th < 300ms at 200 RPS steady state; 95th < 1s during 500 RPS bursts
- Error rate: < 1% (5xx/errors)
- Throughput: support 500 RPS bursts for 45s without queuing > 2s
- Functional quality: pass 7/8 agreed acceptance prompts

I've attached a short POC plan that outlines the test harness and metrics we'll capture (redwood-poc-plan.pdf).

Marissa — can you propose two kickoff slots tomorrow and add a brief agenda (workload walkthrough, integration checklist, procurement blockers)?

Jordan — once you upload the filled intake and sample prompts to the shared drive (link below) we'll lock scheduling.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-poc
Attachment: [attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Jordan — looping in to get the kickoff scheduled and collect the intake artifacts. Proposed times (PST):
- Tue 09 Mar 2027, 11:00-11:45 AM
- Tue 09 Mar 2027, 3:00-3:45 PM

Agenda (30-45m):
- Quick intro + goals (5m)
- Workload intake review (RPS, concurrency, burst patterns, token lengths) (10-15m)
- Integration checklist + credentials (10m)

Workload intake fields we need (please paste or upload into the CSV):

- Peak RPS and typical burst duration

- Typical prompt length and max token context
- Payload size (KB) and downstream latency tolerances

If you can upload the filled CSV and 8 masked sample prompts to the Drive link before the afternoon slot we can start the POC by tomorrow EOD. If procurement needs additional evidence now, cc your procurement contact and we'll start the SOC2/KMS handoff immediately.
